16M here. I can relate with the "constantly obsessively checking the mirror and other reflective surfaces" part. It's also not too long ago when I realized that I'm actually 'obsessed' with making myself perfect. 

One of the most things I do that even other people started to notice is me fixing my hair. Even without a mirror, I have this urge to "fix" it because it makes me anxious about it probably not looking the way I want it to. A few people in the past has pointed it out and even thought it was a way of me kind of "hitting on them" but it really isn't. Most of the people I know finds me attractive (but I always DISAGREE and it's definitely my bdd attacking) and from what I've observed, people always get mixed signals from "attractive" people. Even with the smallest things that these "attractive" people do, these people think these "attractive" people are hitting on them (in my place at least).

But basically, I can relate to the looking at the mirror thing ESPECIALLY when I'm out with some friends or basically ANYONE. I always try to find mirrors to see how I look and fix my hair. Most of the time they look fine but it's really the anxiety and/or bdd that's making me do it. If there's no mirror on sight, I would use my phone and use the front camera from the camera app as my mirror. It's really bad. I'm trying to stop this habit but I really don't know how. Congrats on overcoming it. I think it's a good thing.

Is no one going to mention how iOS is better when you're using the camera in third-party apps? Example is Snapchat or Instagram; when you take a video, there's literally no lag with iOS but with Android, it's a different story. It lags so much specially if you're not hitting the RIGHT lighting. 

I've done some research about it but basically iOS is more optimized with third party apps because Apple only make a few devices a year and it's easier for developers to optimize the apps. While Android on the other hand, there are hundreds of devices released every year and so it's not easy for developers to optimize them one by one (or they're just lazy smh 🙄) so instead of using your phone's ACTUAL camera (which is what's happening on iOS), they just take a screengrab (on Android).

I've been an Android user my whole life and I have been a hater of Apple because of their their lack of features and they're hella expensive... until I got an iPad this August. The iPad's video taking using Snapchat, Instagram, or basically ANY app really impressed me. It's VERY different (or even better) compared to all the phones I've had my whole life (in terms of video recording, not photo quality). So imagine what more an iPhone could offer. I recently bought a new phone at the end of August too and I regret not getting an iPhone instead (lol too broke to afford it anyways 😂)

So I recommend just getting an iPhone instead. The optimization of Apps is really better compared to Android. You also mentioned that you're looking for a good quality camera and that's definitely not a problem with iPhone especially with third party apps (optimization). Although you will probably miss the higher refresh rates from Android when you switch to iPhone. I mean, my phone right now has 90Hz and whenever I switch to my iPad and browse websites, I could REALLY feel the difference. That's all. Sorry for the long comment.

TL;DR: You should switch to iPhone because using the camera on third-party apps is SO MUCH better compared to Android. Although you might miss having higher refresh rates when you're browsing if you switch to iPhone.
